newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia tight-lipped on Saudi bomb suspect.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia tight-lipped on Saudi bomb suspect.

text.p: Saudi Arabia on Wednesday declined to say whether it was seeking the extradition of a Saudi dissident held in Canada for his alleged role in last year's bombing that killed 19 U.S. airmen in the kingdom.

"It is not in the interest of the investigation that I say more than I have," Saudi Interior Minister Prince Nayef told a news conference in Mecca when asked if Riyadh was seeking Hani Abdel-Rahim Hussein al-Sayegh's extradition.
"We do not accuse someone or find them innocent until the investigation is completed," he added.
Sayegh, a Shi'ite Moslem, was arrested in Ottawa last month and charged with having been a driver involved in the June 25 blast in eastern Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia has refused to confirm press reports that it had asked for his extradition.
The Saudi-owned Al-Hayat newspaper last week quoted Sayegh as saying he preferred to stand trial in Saudi Arabia if he was given the choice and assured of what he called "international guarantees".

Sayegh has repeatedly denied any role in the truck bombing. But he has changed his line on where he was at the time of the blast, telling a Canadian newspaper he was in Qom, a key Shi'ite learning centre in Iran, after first saying he was in Syria.

Sayegh, arrested in Ottawa on March 18 on the grounds that he posed a security threat to Canada, arrived in the country appyling for refugee status from Saudi Arabia because of what he said was the way the Sunni Moslem government treated Shi'ites.
An Iranian official has denied a U.S. newspaper report that Iran was harbouring Ahmad Ibrahim Ahmad Mughassil, named by a court document filed in Canada last month as the mastermind of the bombing.
Asked if Sayegh or Mughassil had any links to the attack, Prince Nayef said:
"Concerning what has been published in the media, it (the facts) has to come from an official Saudi source on the record or by the (official) Saudi Press Agency."
Prince Nayef reiterated the Saudi government line that no official conclusions would be made about the truck bombing in the city of al-Khobar until an investigation was concluded.

"With the efforts of the Saudi security men, a lot of information was obtained from the first hour. But as always, the kingdom does not announce anything until the investigation is completed," he said.
